questions.q: For a wave propagating in a medium, identify the property that is independent of the others.

As $v=v \lambda$, the velocity $=$ frequency × wavelength. When light is travelling in a medium, $v$ is assumed to be the same and the velocity of light in the medium is less. $\lambda$ gets adjusted so that $\frac{c^{\prime}}{\lambda^{\prime}}=v$. Here $v$ is independent.

questions.q: A string vibrates with a frequency of $200 \mathrm{~Hz}$. When its length is doubled and tension is altered, it begins to vibrate with a frequency of $300 \mathrm{~Hz}$. The ratio of the new tension to the original tension is
questions.solution:
The fundamental frequency of a vibrating string is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $L$ is the length, $T$ is the tension, and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

Let the initial frequency be $f_1 = 200 \text{ Hz}$, length be $L_1 = L$, and tension be $T_1$. Then $f_1 = \dfrac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{\mu}}$.

Let the new frequency be $f_2 = 300 \text{ Hz}$, new length be $L_2 = 2L$, and new tension be $T_2$. Then $f_2 = \dfrac{1}{2(2L)} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{\mu}} = \dfrac{1}{4L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{\mu}}$.

Taking the ratio of the two frequencies:

$\dfrac{f_2}{f_1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{\mu}}}{\dfrac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{\mu}}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}}$.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{300}{200} = \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}}$.

Multiplying both sides by 2:

$3 = \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}}$.

Squaring both sides:

$9 = \dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$.

Therefore, the ratio of the new tension to the original tension is $9:1$.

Answer: 9 : 1

questions.q: Two monochromatic coherent light beams $A$ and $B$ have intensities $L$ and $\frac{L}{4},$ respectively. If these beams are superposed, the maximum and minimum intensities will be
questions.solution:
For maximum intensity,

I_{\max }=I_{1}+I_{2}+2 \sqrt{I_{1} I_{2}} \cos \delta

\begin{aligned}
\delta &=0 \\
I_{\max } &=L+\frac{L}{4}+2 \sqrt{L \times \frac{L}{4}} \cdot \cos 0 \\
&=\frac{5 L}{4}+\frac{2 L}{2} \\
&=\frac{5 L+4 L}{4} \\
&=\frac{9 L}{4} \\
I_{\min } &=I_{1}+I_{2}-2 \sqrt{I_{1} I_{2}} \cos \theta \\
\theta &=0^{\circ} \\
&=L+\frac{L}{4}-2 \sqrt{L \times \frac{L}{4}} \times 1 \\
&=\frac{5 L}{4}-L=\frac{L}{4}
\end{aligned}

Thus, maximum and minimum intensities will be $\left(\frac{9 L}{4}, \frac{L}{4}\right)$

questions.q: A wave packet with center frequency $\omega$ is propagating in dispersive medium with phase velocity of $1.5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. When the frequency $\omega$ is increased by $2 \%$, the phase velocity is found to decrease by $3 \%$. What is the group velocity of the wave packet?
questions.solution:
Phase velocity, $v_p=\frac{\omega}{k}\begin{aligned} & \frac{d v_p}{v_p}=\frac{d \omega}{\omega}-\frac{d k}{k} \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{d k}{k}=\frac{d \omega}{\omega}-\frac{d v_p}{v_p}=2 \%-(-3 \%)=5 \%\end{aligned}$
Group velocity, $v_g=\frac{d \omega}{d k}\begin{aligned} & \frac{d \omega}{d k}=v_p\left(\frac{d \omega / \omega}{d k / k}\right)=1.5 \times 10^3\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) \\ & =0.6 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Paragraph: Two plane harmonic sound waves are expressed by the equations. \begin{aligned} & y_1(x, t)=A \cos (0.5 \pi x-100 \pi t) \\ & y_2(x, t)=A \cos (0.46 \pi x-92 \pi t) \end{aligned} (All parameters are in MKS)Question: At $x=0$ how many times the amplitude of $y_1+y_2$ is zero in one second at $x=0$ ?
questions.solution:
At $x=0, y=y_1+y_2=2 A \cos 96 \pi t \cos 4 \pi t$
Frequency of $\cos (96 \pi t)$ function is $48 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and that of $\cos (4 \pi t)$ function is $2 \mathrm{~Hz}$. In one second cos function becomes zero at $2 f$ times, where $f$ is the frequency. Therefore, first function will become zero at 96 times and the second at 4 times. But second overlaps with first. Hence, net $y$ will become zero 96 times in 1 second.

questions.q:
Four light sources produce the following four waves :
(i) $y_1=a \sin \left(\omega t+\phi_1\right)$
(ii) $y_2=a \sin 2 \omega t$
(iii) $y_3=d^{\prime} \sin \left(\omega t+\phi_2\right)$
(iv) $y_4=d^{\prime} \sin (3 \omega t+\phi)$
Superposition of which two waves give rise to interference?
questions.solution:
Interference phenomenon takes place between two waves which have equal frequency and propagate in same direction.
Hence,
$\begin{aligned}
& y_1=a \sin \left(\omega t+\phi_1\right) \\
& y_3=d^{\prime} \sin \left(\omega t+\phi_2\right)
\end{aligned}$
will give rise to interference as the two waves have same frequency $\omega$.
